title: The Undercover Economist
summary: Economics explained through everyday questions, from who pays for your coffee to why poor countries are poor: prices reveal scarcity and value, and institutions matter more than policies. In the end, economics is about people.

title: Data Science for Business
summary: Less technical depth than Vanderplas, but a good overview of the recurring problems in data science for business. The expected-value framework is very useful.

title: Doing Data Science
summary: Not worth it. No business acumen, no technical insights: only guest lectures from a class.

title: Storytelling with Data
summary: Useful information, but diluted over a book when it could be a blog post.

title: Carrie
summary: A fun story to read: a girl with telekinetic powers gets pissed, and destroys the town where she lives.

title: The Wonderful Story of Henry Sugar (Plus)
summary: Henry Sugar finds a way to see without the eyes. Plus six more stories.

title: Charles Darwin: A Life from Beginning to End
summary: Darwin (1809–1882) came from a privileged family. Not brilliant in school, but persistent in his curiosity and method. And lucky.

title: The Black Death
summary: The bubonic plague (1345–1353) in one hour. It killed about one third of the European and Asian population.

title: How to Travel with a Salmon
summary: Funny short read.

title: A Short History of Nearly Everything
summary: If you're interested in history and science, you must read this book. Bryson explains how scientific ideas came about, and how the people who came up with them were often special human beings.

title: Reinventing Discovery
summary: Read half of it, then stopped. It has some interesting points, but it can be quite verbose for what I get out of it.

title: What Color is Your Parachute?
summary: Somewhat useful to force you to think about what you want.

title: How to Win Friends and Influence People
Physics for Future Presidents: The Science Behind the Headlines
The Lessons of History
summary: History in a hundred pages: biology, morals, religion, economics and war. Progress is the increasing control of the environment by life, and equal educational opportunity is the best a fair society can offer.

title: Letters from a Self-Made Merchant to His Son Being the Letters written by John Graham, Head of the House of Graham & Company, Pork-Packers in Chicago, ... known to his intimates as "Piggy."
summary: A bit dated (sometimes it can be racist), but most of it is wise and pragmatic.

title: How to Read a Book
summary: Good book, should be read in high school. Start from the basics (title, table of contents), read carefully or move on, skim, underline, annotate.

title: Atoms in the Family
summary: Biography of Enrico Fermi written by his wife. He was very competitive, even with his wife, a bit macho (not surprising for someone born in 1901), and super smart.

title: How to Make Sense of Any Mess
summary: Lots of fluff, no content.

title: On Human Nature
summary: What defines a human being, and how much of it comes from evolutionary biology? Some things it said crystal clear that I already thought; others it changed my view on.

title: Les enfants des justes
summary: In Nazi-occupied France, Virgile and Victoria, two simple people, take care of two Jewish kids. Mi ricorda molto Fenoglio: una scrittura schietta e semplice.

title: Against the Fall of Night (Arthur C. Clarke Collection
summary: Really good sci-fi novel. A gate is found that connects a society with the forgotten outside world.

title: The Rosie Project: A Novel (Don Tillman Book 1)
summary: A Sheldon-Cooper-type professor sets up a questionnaire to find the best life partner, and falls for someone who fits none of the criteria. Funny and smart.

title: Une si belle école
summary: Primary school teachers in post-war rural France, where school is a duty that harsh conditions keep people from appreciating. It reminds me of the life my parents went through.

title: Rules of the Game
summary: Follow-up of The Game. Not as entertaining.

title: Get-It-Done Guy's 9 Steps to Work Less and Do More
Thinking, Fast and Slow
summary: Our brain behaves as if there were two actors: a fast, intuitive one shaped by evolution, and a slow, rational one. Their interaction leads to systematic biases, and the only defence is to train yourself to recognize them.

title: Bonk: The Curious Coupling of Science and Sex
summary: The science of sex, from animals to humans, from bed to MRI. Interesting and humorous.

title: The Flinch
summary: We are used to being comfortable. Sometimes it's good to take risks, and the way to do it rationally is to train yourself to flinch.

title: The Game
summary: Pick-up artists' adventures. An interesting perspective on human interactions, and on how we are programmed to react.

title: Working Effectively with Legacy Code (Robert C. Martin Series)
summary: Legacy code is always there, you have to deal with it: unit testing, strategies to refactor, strategies to clean up. Very useful.

title: Shackleton's Way: Leadership Lessons from the Great Antarctic Explorer
summary: Epic. The story of a captain and a leader.

title: Megawatts and Megatons
summary: Plenty of useful numbers and facts. Perhaps a bit outdated, but still very interesting.

title: La vie à fil tendu
summary: Short and well written. Two parts: the human being and the scientist.

title: Fooled by Randomness
summary: Randomness is there in the markets, so there's very little we can do to predict them; realizing it protects you from easy-gain fairy tales. Good read.

title: Notes to a Software Team Leader
summary: Good book, but I don't remember anything. Look at the notes.

title: The Varieties of Scientific Experience
summary: Wonderful and humbling: science framed within the cosmos, then what it means to have a religious experience. Sagan makes simple, crystal-clear points, without preconceptions, and treats believers with respect, almost tenderness. It should be read in schools.

title: Dreams in a Time of War: A Childhood Memoir
summary: Ngugi grows up in rural Kenya in 1934–1950 and, despite poverty, war, colonialism and racism, manages to go to school: the support people give each other makes apparently impossible dreams happen.

title: The Ultimate Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
summary: Fun. 42. Don't panic.

title: Foundation
summary: One of the best sci-fi I've ever read. Science in the future is so advanced that it can predict when revolutions and changes will happen.

title: Night (Night Trilogy)
summary: Humanity pushed to its limits.

title: The Practice of Programming
summary: Habits and tips that seem common sense once you see them written down: good naming, clean interfaces, systematic testing, profile before optimizing. This book should be read by everyone writing code.

title: The Life You Can Save
summary: Compelling: poverty in the world has jaw-dropping figures, you are in a privileged top 1%, and a solution is possible if you play your role. After reading it you won't look at your problems the same way.

title: Lettere di condannati a morte della Resistenza italiana. 8 settembre 1943-25 aprile 1945
Ultime lettere di condannati a morte e di deportati della resistenza (Italian Edition)
L'Étranger
summary: Uno dei libri migliori che abbia letto. Una trama breve e scarna, ma un libro che fa pensare molto, e che colpisce al ventre quando meno te lo aspetti.

title: Brave New World
summary: A dystopia driven by pragmatism and coldness: family ties reduced to the minimum, emotions regarded as dangerous, happiness ensured by the state with drugs. Its strength is how accurately it describes that future society.

title: Il mondo dei vinti
summary: 85 testimonianze dei poveri delle campagne cuneesi, raccolte nel 1970–72: un secolo di storia, dall'unità d'Italia allo sbarco sulla Luna, raccontato dai vinti. Un quadro completamente diverso da quello studiato a scuola.
